chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Fadalah from Jamil who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted: 'So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who is righteous' (Q53:32). He said: 'It is when a person says: I prayed last night and I fasted yesterday, and similar to this.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, some people would say in the mornings: We prayed last night and we fasted yesterday.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'But as for me, I sleep at night and during the day, and if I could find any time between them, I would have slept in it as well.'

key_terms.فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنفُسَكُمْ: Do not claim yourselves to be pure (Quranic phrase)
key_terms.هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقَىٰ: He is most knowing of who is righteous (Quranic phrase)
key_terms.يُصْبِحُونَ: They would say in the mornings

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'Fala tuzakku anfusakum' mean in the context of showing off in worship?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'So do not claim yourselves to be pure' (Q53:32) specifically targets the internal vanity of boasting about one's worship, such as saying 'I prayed last night.' This is contrasted with Imam Ali (AS), who humbly attributed his lack of night prayer to sleep rather than pride, illustrating that true piety avoids self-advertisement. The hadith highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) over the mere quantity of acts, warning against the subtle corruption of the heart by self-admiration.
